q: Pictured: bedroom. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Cuarto, Alcoba, Dormitorio” is the vernacular for bedroom. Origin: cuarto is “quarter, room”; alcoba is from Arabic al-qubba; dormitorio is from dormir “to sleep”, like English “dormitory”.

q: Pictured: bath tub. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Baniera / Banyera” is the vernacular for bath tub. Origin: Spanish bañera “bathtub”, from baño “bath”.

q: Pictured: storeroom. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Bodega” is the vernacular for storeroom. Origin: Spanish bodega “storeroom, wine cellar”, from Latin apotheca.

q: Pictured: bath. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Bano” is the vernacular for bath. Origin: Spanish baño “bath”. The Spanish letter ñ is written n here.

q: Pictured: balcony. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Balcon” is the vernacular for balcony. Origin: Spanish balcón, borrowed from Italian balcone. Same word as English “balcony”.

q: Pictured: toilet. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Letrina / Comun” is the vernacular for toilet. Origin: letrina is Spanish “latrine” (Latin latrina); común is “common, shared”.

q: Pictured: showerhead. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Ducha” is the vernacular for showerhead. Origin: Spanish ducha “shower”, borrowed from French douche.

q: Pictured: hall. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Caida” is the vernacular for hall. Borrowed from Spanish caída “fall, drop”. In the traditional bahay na bato it typically names the hall at the head of the stairs.

q: Pictured: caulking cotton (oakum). Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Estopa” is the vernacular for caulking cotton (oakum). Origin: Spanish estopa “tow”, the coarse fibre used to caulk joints.

q: Pictured: pantry. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Dispensa” is the vernacular for pantry. Origin: Spanish despensa/dispensa “pantry”, from dispensar “to hand out provisions”. Related to English “dispense”.

q: Pictured: dish rack. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Bangguerahan” is the vernacular for dish rack. Memory aid: I couldn't confirm the root. The suffix -han marks a place for something, as in lutuan, so it is the place where dishes are kept.

q: Pictured: dining room. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Comedor” is the vernacular for dining room. Origin: Spanish comedor, from comer “to eat”.

q: Pictured: lavatory. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Lababo” is the vernacular for lavatory. Origin: Spanish lavabo “washbasin”, from lavar “to wash”. Related to English “lavatory”.

q: Pictured: low table. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Dulang” is the vernacular for low table. Origin: native Tagalog dulang, a low dining table or tray.

q: Pictured: water closet. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Inodoro” is the vernacular for water closet. Origin: Spanish inodoro “toilet”, literally in- “without” + odor, so odourless.

q: Pictured: water cistern. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Aljibe” is the vernacular for water cistern. Origin: Spanish aljibe “cistern”, from Arabic al-jubb “the well”.

q: Pictured: kitchen. Which vernacular term names it?
ref: Know-How Architecture, “Building Technology: Construction Vernacular Terms” (#InstaFlashCards): term and image.
n: “Cocina” is the vernacular for kitchen. Origin: Spanish cocina, from Latin coquina “cooking”. Related to English “cuisine”.
